extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required items for reviewing submissions to the NAACL‑HLT 2021 conference, covering what to include in the review, scoring rubrics (reproducibility, ethics, overall recommendation), and procedural expectations (supplementary material, secondary reviewers, author response).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of any submission to the NAACL‑HLT 2021 conference, any discussion of such submissions as well as the names of participants in such discussions are confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose submission content or discussion participants outside the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core review (main contributions and evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the most important part. It should include your view of the main contributions that the paper intended to make and how well it succeeds at making these contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain significant strong and weak parts of the paper and the work it describes; describe how the work advances the state of knowledge in computational linguistics and/or why it fails to make a sufficient contribution. This could be a 2 paragraph (or longer) essay and/or bullet points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to accept
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize from your core review the main reasons why this paper should be accepted for the conference, and how the NLP community would benefit from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may refer back to your core review to provide more context and details; tie benefits to community and advancement of knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the main reasons that this paper cannot be published and presented in its current form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify parts that would need to be improved to advance the state of knowledge; be concrete about fatal flaws or gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions and additional feedback for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Place for questions you would like the authors to respond to during the author response period and suggestions to help authors improve the paper for the final version (or a future submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to solicit clarifications and to provide constructive suggestions that authors can address in the rebuttal or revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility — rating of paper reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: How do you rate the paper’s reproducibility? Will members of the ACL community be able to reproduce or verify the results in this paper? (Scores of 1–5; N/A for papers without empirical results.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the detailed explanation for each point level provided in the review form; consider code, data, experimental detail, and clarity of method descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility checklist usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the authors’ answers to the Reproducibility Checklist useful for evaluating the submission? (three choices: very useful, somewhat useful, not useful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This question is to collect feedback on the checklist itself and is not a direct evaluation of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review / broader impact statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag papers for ethical concerns; papers working with sensitive data or on sensitive tasks that do not discuss these issues will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors were allowed extra space after page limits for a broader impact or ethics discussion. Read the ethics FAQ for guidance on problems to look out for; papers lacking necessary ethical discussion should be flagged for further review by an ethics committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation (numeric scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesize the above and provide an overall recommendation using a 5‑point scale with half‑point increments (including an allowed rating of 3 = ambivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are not made solely on scores; align your numeric recommendation with the reasoning in your core review so authors and area chairs can understand the motivation. If borderline, use 3; otherwise try to take a stand (e.g., 2.5 or 3.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform the committee and authors how confident you are about your recommendation, taking into account your expertise and familiarity with this area and the paper’s contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use confidence to contextualize the strength of your recommendation and whether you feel qualified to judge the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations for Best Long/Short/Theme Paper and outstanding paper awards; nominators must provide justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open‑minded and nominate a wide variety of paper types (surveys, opinion, resources, low‑resource language work, analyses). Note: unlike previous conferences, if you recommend a paper for an award, the authors will see your comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential information to area/PC chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: A section for confidential comments to area chairs and/or PC chairs that will not be shared with authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this for sensitive internal remarks that should not be visible to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response follow‑up
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be an author response period; check whether author responses clear up your questions or misunderstandings and update your recommendation and core review accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If author responses influence your decision, update the review and explicitly state any new decisions so Area Chairs are aware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials — treatment and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary materials are allowed as a stand‑alone document uploaded as an additional file and are supplementary; you have no obligation to read them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat them like other citations that may help understand background/details beyond the paper; given reproducibility requirements, authors may provide appendices and zip files with code/data — please take some time to check those if applicable. Uploading data/code is preferred to hyperlinks to avoid double‑blind violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary reviewers / external help
rubrics_metrics.description: You are allowed to solicit help from others; however, the final review and scores must reflect your own opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take the secondary reviewer’s review and rewrite it using your own words and adjust scores as you see fit. Be prepared to justify the final review as your own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format violations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Program chairs and area chairs have desk‑rejected submissions that violated formatting guidelines; you should not need to worry about formatting issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find formatting violations that were missed and believe the paper violates format guidelines, contact your area chairs or PCs. Otherwise, do not down‑weight evaluation for minor formatting issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision process context — scores are not sole factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions will be made not just on the scores (and certainly not on average scores), but will also take into account the whole review, reviewer discussion and Area Chair meta‑reviews and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide coherent reasoning that aligns with your recommendation so authors and ACs can understand how decisions should be arrived at.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will be instructed to flag poor reviews, ask reviewers to revise their reviews or provide objective reasons to justify positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow guidance on writing high quality reviews; expect to be asked to revise if reviews are judged poor or not sufficiently justified.
